facts.q: Who determines that a student is of good moral character for enrollment?

facts.text: To enroll, a student must be physically qualified to take full part in the school's physical education program. A current annual school physical is mandatory.
facts.q: What physical standard must a cadet meet to enroll?
facts.a: Physically qualified to take full part in the school's physical education program

facts.text: A cadet may be disenrolled for academic failure, ineptitude or poor attitude.
facts.q: What are the three reasons the handbook gives for disenrollment?
facts.a: Academic failure, ineptitude and poor attitude

facts.text: Disenrollment for failing MCJROTC is not automatic. Each case is reviewed and handled separately.
facts.q: Is disenrollment for academic failure automatic?
facts.a: No. Each case is reviewed separately.

facts.text: A cadet who fails to maintain the minimum GPA set by the SMI and approved by the principal is placed on probation during the next semester.
facts.q: What happens when a cadet falls below the minimum GPA?

facts.text: A cadet on academic probation who does not raise the GPA during the next semester is suspended from MCJROTC and must turn in all uniforms.
facts.q: What happens if a cadet on academic probation does not raise the GPA?
facts.a: Suspension from MCJROTC and turn-in of all uniforms

facts.text: The MCJROTC curriculum is called Leadership Education.
facts.q: What is the MCJROTC curriculum called?

facts.text: Leadership Education has five categories: Leadership; Citizenship; Personal Growth and Responsibility; Public Service and Career Exploration; and General Military Subjects.
facts.q: What are the five categories of Leadership Education?
facts.a: Leadership; Citizenship; Personal Growth and Responsibility; Public Service and Career Exploration; General Military Subjects

facts.text: LE-II introduces civilian marksmanship training and land navigation with map and compass.
facts.q: Which Leadership Education level introduces marksmanship and land navigation?

facts.text: In LE-III cadets take positions of increased authority, and receive detailed instruction on personal finances.
facts.q: Which Leadership Education level gives detailed instruction on personal finances?

facts.text: LE-IV cadets conduct formations and inspections and supervise training of younger cadets.
facts.q: In which Leadership Education level do cadets conduct formations and inspections?

facts.text: Part of the MCJROTC grade is leadership performance: carrying out cadet duties and taking part in citizenship and other MCJROTC activities.
facts.q: Besides academics, what is a cadet graded on?

facts.text: Cadets are expected to attend all JROTC functions, and to tell the instructors in advance when they cannot.
facts.q: What should a cadet do when unable to attend a JROTC function?

facts.text: Cadets are expected to follow all school rules and regulations.
facts.q: Whose rules must cadets follow in addition to the unit's?

facts.text: After roll call the class commander gives the command "Ready, seats". The class sits at attention until given "At ease".
facts.q: What command does the class commander give after roll call?

facts.text: When recognized or asked a question, a cadet stands while speaking.
facts.q: What does a cadet do when recognized to speak in class?

facts.text: Cadets use "Sir" or "Ma'am" when addressing or answering the SMI or MI.
facts.q: How does a cadet address the SMI or MI?

facts.text: Head calls are made before or after class, except in an emergency.
facts.q: When are head calls made?
facts.a: Before or after class, except in an emergency

facts.text: Safety is first and foremost in MCJROTC marksmanship, in the classroom and on a competitive team.
facts.q: What comes first in MCJROTC marksmanship?

facts.text: All qualification firing is done with the Sporter air rifle.
facts.q: Which rifle is used for qualification firing?

facts.text: Air rifle qualification firing is done at a distance of 10 meters (33 feet).
facts.q: At what distance is air rifle qualification fired?

facts.text: Marksman: 10 shots standing and 10 shots prone, scoring 110 to 129.
facts.q: What score range earns the Marksman badge?

facts.text: Sharpshooter: 10 shots standing and 10 shots prone, scoring 130 to 200.
facts.q: What score range earns the Sharpshooter badge?

facts.text: Expert: 10 shots each prone, standing and kneeling, fired at the same time, scoring 221 to 300.
facts.q: What score range earns the Expert badge?

facts.text: The Expert badge requires qualification firing in all three positions: prone, standing and kneeling.
facts.q: Which firing positions does the Expert badge require?

facts.text: A physical fitness test is given twice a year and is one of the requirements for promotion.
facts.q: How often is the physical fitness test given?

facts.text: YPFT first class is 350 to 500 points.
facts.q: What YPFT score range is first class?

facts.text: YPFT second class is 250 to 349 points.
facts.q: What YPFT score range is second class?

facts.text: YPFT third class is 150 to 249 points.
facts.q: What YPFT score range is third class?

facts.text: A YPFT score below 150 points is failing.
facts.q: Below what YPFT score does a cadet fail?

facts.text: Ribbons are worn in order of precedence with the senior ribbon on top and to the wearer's right.
facts.q: Where does the senior ribbon go?
facts.a: On top and to the wearer's right
distractors: On top and to the wearer's left
On the bottom and to the wearer's right
In the center of the bottom row

facts.text: Ribbons are worn 1/8 inch above and centered over the left breast pocket of the khaki shirt or blue coat.
facts.q: How far above the left breast pocket are ribbons worn?

facts.text: When ribbons are worn with the marksmanship badge, the ribbons sit 1/8 inch above the badge.
facts.q: Where do ribbons sit when the marksmanship badge is also worn?

facts.text: Authorized medals are worn on the blue coat when the training schedule prescribes them, over the left breast pocket, midway between the first and second buttons.
facts.q: On which uniform item are medals worn?

facts.text: When medals are worn, ribbons that have no medal are worn 1/8 inch above and centered over the right breast pocket.
facts.q: When medals are worn, where do ribbons without a medal go?
facts.a: 1/8 inch above and centered over the right breast pocket

facts.text: When ribbons are on the right side, the nametag is worn 1/8 inch above the ribbon bar.
facts.q: Where is the nametag worn when ribbons are on the right side?

facts.text: Authorized badges are worn 1/8 inch above and centered over the left breast pocket of the khaki shirt and blue coat.
facts.q: Where are authorized badges worn?
facts.a: 1/8 inch above and centered over the left breast pocket

facts.text: A cadet may wear one marksmanship badge, for the classification earned at the most recent range qualification.
facts.q: How many marksmanship badges may a cadet wear?
facts.a: One, for the most recent qualification

facts.text: Marksmanship badges are not worn when medals are worn on the blue coat.
facts.q: May a marksmanship badge be worn with medals on the blue coat?

facts.text: Ribbons and badges are not normally worn during the school day. They are worn for prescribed events and are authorized on leave and liberty.
facts.q: Are ribbons and badges normally worn during the school day?
facts.a: No. They are worn for prescribed events.

facts.text: All other awards are worn after the listed JROTC awards, and must be approved by the Marine Corps JROTC Program Office before being worn.
facts.q: Who must approve an award that is not on the handbook list before it is worn?
facts.a: The Marine Corps JROTC Program Office

facts.text: Marksmanship qualification badges have three levels: Marksman, Sharpshooter and Expert. Expert is the highest.
facts.q: Which marksmanship qualification badge is the highest?

facts.text: Cadets scoring more than 250 points on the Youth Physical Fitness Test are awarded the Physical Fitness Achievement Ribbon and the National Youth Physical Fitness Program Certificate.
facts.q: What YPFT score earns the Physical Fitness Achievement Ribbon?

facts.text: Blue Dress "Bravo": blue trousers or skirt with blue coat, ribbons only.
facts.q: Which uniform is blue trousers or skirt with the blue coat, ribbons only?

facts.text: Blue Dress "Charlie": blue trousers or skirt with khaki long sleeve shirt and tie.
facts.q: Which uniform is blue trousers or skirt with khaki long sleeve shirt and tie?

facts.text: Blue Dress "Delta": blue trousers or skirt with khaki short sleeve shirt.
facts.q: Which uniform is blue trousers or skirt with khaki short sleeve shirt?

facts.text: Service "Alpha": green trousers or skirt with green coat and long sleeve shirt.
facts.q: Which uniform is green trousers or skirt with the green coat and long sleeve shirt?

facts.text: Service "Bravo": green trousers or skirt with khaki long sleeve shirt and tie.
facts.q: Which uniform is green trousers or skirt with khaki long sleeve shirt and tie?

facts.text: Service "Charlie": green trousers or skirt with khaki short sleeve shirt.
facts.q: Which uniform is green trousers or skirt with khaki short sleeve shirt?

facts.text: Utility Uniform: camouflage blouse and trousers.
facts.q: Which uniform is the camouflage blouse and trousers?

facts.text: The web belt extends between 2 and 4 inches past the buckle.
facts.q: How far past the buckle does the web belt extend?

facts.text: The cloth belt extends between 2 3/4 and 3 3/4 inches past the buckle.
facts.q: How far past the buckle does the cloth belt extend?

facts.text: Military alignment: the shirt edge, belt buckle and fly of the trousers are in one straight vertical line.
facts.q: Which three things form the straight vertical line called military alignment?
facts.a: Shirt edge, belt buckle and fly of the trousers

facts.text: The tie clasp is centered between the 3rd and 4th button on the long sleeve shirt.
facts.q: Where is the tie clasp worn?
distractors: Even with the top of the pockets

facts.text: The bottom of the trousers is even with the welt where the heel and sole of the shoe join.
facts.q: Where does the bottom of the trousers fall?
facts.a: Even with the welt where the heel and sole of the shoe join

facts.text: Skirt length approximates the knee, no more than 1 inch above or below the center of the knee.
facts.q: How far above or below the center of the knee may the skirt fall?

facts.text: The cover is never worn indoors.
facts.q: Is the cover worn indoors?
facts.a: No. It is never worn indoors.

facts.text: On the cover, the wings of the emblem are parallel to the deck and the anchor points forward.
facts.q: On the cover, which way does the anchor of the emblem point?

facts.text: On the Service "Alpha" and blues, the left and right collar emblems are worn parallel to the deck with the anchors pointed inboard.
facts.q: On the collar, which way do the anchors of the emblems point?

facts.text: Enlisted insignia of grade is worn 1/2 inch from the collar edge and centered on the collar, point of the chevron up, bisecting the angle of the collar.
facts.q: How far from the collar edge is enlisted insignia of grade worn?

facts.text: Officer insignia of grade is worn 1 inch from the collar edge on the centerline of the collar.
facts.q: How far from the front collar edge is officer insignia of grade worn?

facts.text: Cadet officers wear rank insignia centered on the shoulder strap of the blue coat and all weather coats.
facts.q: Where do cadet officers wear rank insignia on the blue coat?
distractors: On the collar, 1 inch from the edge

facts.text: Cloth embroidered rank insignia for enlisted cadets is worn only on the blue coat.
facts.q: On which item do enlisted cadets wear cloth embroidered rank insignia?

facts.text: With the utility uniform, rank insignia is worn on the front of the utility cap.
facts.q: Where is rank insignia worn on the utility cover?
facts.a: On the front of the utility cap

facts.text: The Marine Corps JROTC shoulder patch is worn on the left sleeve of the blue coat, green coat, khaki shirt and camouflage utility jacket.
facts.q: On which sleeve is the MCJROTC shoulder patch worn?
distractors: Neither. It is worn on the pocket.

facts.text: Male cadets: hair is tapered in the back, does not fall over the ears or eyebrows, and does not interfere with the cover. Sideburns are neatly trimmed and no longer than the opening of the ear.
facts.q: How long may a male cadet's sideburns be?
facts.a: No longer than the opening of the ear

facts.text: Male cadets are clean-shaven, except that a neatly trimmed moustache may be worn.
facts.q: What facial hair may a male cadet wear?

facts.text: Female cadets in uniform: hair is pinned and arranged so it does not fall below the collar, and so the cover can be worn properly.
facts.q: In uniform, how low may a female cadet's hair fall?
facts.a: Not below the collar of the uniform

facts.text: Female cadets may wear one small, polished ball or round stud earring per ear, no more than 1/4 inch in diameter, with all uniforms except camouflage. Earrings are not worn in parades, reviews or ceremonies.
facts.q: What is the largest earring diameter allowed?

facts.text: Cadets wear the uniform at least one day a week. The Senior Marine Instructor sets the day.
facts.q: How often must cadets wear the uniform, at a minimum?
facts.a: At least one day a week
distractors: At least two days a week

facts.text: In uniform, wear your cover outdoors at all times and remove it indoors.
facts.q: In uniform, when is the cover worn?
facts.a: Outdoors at all times; removed indoors

facts.text: In uniform, do not chew gum, do not smoke, and do not walk or stand with your hands in your pockets.
facts.q: Name three things the handbook says not to do in uniform.
facts.a: Chew gum, smoke, or put your hands in your pockets

facts.text: Camouflage uniforms and cotton T-shirts are washed in warm or cold water only.
facts.q: Which uniform items may be machine washed?

facts.text: Khaki shirts, poly-wool green trousers, wool sweaters and dress coats must be dry-cleaned, not washed.
facts.q: How are khaki shirts, green trousers, wool sweaters and dress coats cleaned?

facts.text: Cadets are responsible for their uniforms. Replacing a lost, stolen or damaged uniform is the financial responsibility of the cadet.
facts.q: Who pays to replace a lost, stolen or damaged uniform?
